messages:
Anya: Quick UX review — compact capacity card feels dense when SLO slider is visible. Thoughts?
Mike: Agree. On small screens the min/max steppers + burst pill push the model name off the card.
Deepa: Proposed: collapse the SLO rail into an overflow chevron and show summary badge 'SLO: 99ms' — tap expands inline.
Oliver: Concern: hiding SLO by default makes guardrails less discoverable during onboarding. Maybe show a soft-outline when SLO deviates.
Anya: Good point. What if we show a subtle red/amber dot on the card when guardrail is active and keep SLO collapsed?
DesignBot: mockup uploaded — /files/figma? In thread: https://redwood.app/figma/capacity-compact-rail
Mike: Keyboard flow: tab order currently goes model -> min -> max -> burst -> add-pool. Need to surface SLO toggle before burst.
Deepa: Also aria: the burst pill has no aria-label describing 'burst capacity' or its units. Screen reader says 'button'.
Anya: Accessibility nit: color contrast of the SLO slider track in the 'good' state is 3.8:1. Needs to be >=4.5:1.
Oliver: Copy tweak: change 'Burst' tooltip to 'Burst capacity — temporary extra GPUs' and add 'expires in Xm' in expanded view.
Deepa: On pool switch, current animation is too long (500ms). Causes layout jumping. Suggest 200ms fade + scale.
Mike: UX question: if pool is incompatible (no preemptible on requested SLAs), do we disable pool in picker or allow selection with inline warning?
Anya: Prefer allow selection + inline warning + automatic fallback toggle (opt-in). That aligns with graceful degradation.
Oliver: Edge: when min==max, autoscale should show 'fixed capacity' badge instead of a disabled slider.
DesignBot: Updated figma with ARIA labels, reduced contrast, and collapsed SLO states. link: https://redwood.app/figma/abc123
Anya: Next steps: Deepa to create accessibility PR for aria-labels + contrast; Mike to prototype pool-switch animation; Oliver to write microcopy changes. Meeting tomorrow 10:30 PT?
Mike: +1
Deepa: On it. I'll put the WIP PR link in #design-review when ready.
Anya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
